question: The French attempt to challenge English influence in Bengal during the Seven Years' War collapsed when the British captured Chandernagore in March 1757. Which of the following describes the key factors that facilitated this capture?
options: The Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, actively joined the British forces in bombarding the French fort
Siraj-ud-Daulah was bribed by Clive, and the French commander at Chandernagore defected to the British
Siraj-ud-Daulah, distracted by threats of an Afghan invasion and pressured by Admiral Watson and Robert Clive, remained neutral while the British fleet sailed up the Hooghly River to bombard the fort
The French troops under Bussy were recalled to Pondicherry to defend it against a Maratha attack
explanation: In March 1757, Robert Clive and Admiral Watson decided to attack Chandernagore to eliminate French influence in Bengal before dealing with Siraj-ud-Daulah. Siraj-ud-Daulah was worried about an invasion by Ahmad Shah Abdali from the north and did not want to alienate the British. Consequently, he failed to assist the French effectively and remained neutral, allowing Watson's warships to sail up the Hooghly and bombard Fort d'Orleans, leading to its surrender.
